newsitem.title: USA: White House to draft trade bill by summer - McCurry.
newsitem.headline: White House to draft trade bill by summer - McCurry.

text.p: White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Wednesday the administration plans to send to Congress proposed trade negotiation legislation by late spring or summer.

"I don't think it has been pinpointed yet partly because we have to do the China (Most Favored Nation) piece," he told Reuters. "We got the balanced budget agreement, then we got a China MFN piece and then we've got to figure out when you do the fast track thing."

Supporters of the so-called fast track trade negotiation legislation have been anxiously awaiting proposed legislation from the administration. But a dispute between Republicans and Democrats over whether it should include authority to negotiate labor and environmental issues in trade deals has held up the proposal.

Administration officials have been trying to work out a compromise that would win both Democratic and Republican votes and Congressional supporters are beginning to worry that the administration would wait until later this year or next year to submit a proposed bill.
Fast track authority is needed to negotiate an expansion of the North American Free Trade Agreement to include Chile, as well as other trade deals.

It would allow U.S. officials to negotiate trade agreements without fear the details will be changed by Congress. Lawmakers could vote either yes or no on a treaty negotiated with fast-track authority, but could not vote to approve only part of it and demand amendments to other parts.
House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer, R-Texas, who had hoped to deal with the trade legislation early in the year, expressed dismay at the delay.

"It's very unfortunate that the administration is unable to give what should be a major trade priority -- early renewal of fast track -- the attention it deserves," Archer said in a statement. He expressed concern that the White House will postpone consideration of the legislation until next year.
But McCurry said the White House is not trying to delay the trade legislation.
"To the contrary, you've got Republicans on the Hill who are looking to jump start the whole thing before we're actually ready because we don't have enough ducks lined up right now," McCurry said.
"We've been going to them and saying look don't -- the system can only bear so much at a time."

Earlier on Tuesday, during the regular White House briefing, McCurry said he hoped Congressional consideration of fast track would be well under way by October and that the negotiation authority would be in place by the time the leaders of the Americas meet in Santiago, Chile in March 1998.
"I think he would like it done before he goes to Santiago for the second Summit of the Americas, so that you can then present to them the launch," McCurry said.
